scope: borrowed per-port queue slices instead of cloning Vec<Arc<BoundedQueue>> in named recv/recv_timeout
per-port edge cursor sharing with recv_any/recv_any_timeout
assessment: No concrete non-security correctness blocker found in the product delta. The named helper starts from the existing per-port cursor, scans the same queue order, and advances that cursor only when it dequeues an event (src/graph/transport.rs:471-492); the existing mixed-method regression demonstrates cursor continuity across named and any-input calls (lines 2960-3042). The single-queue blocking path retains the same cancellation-token receive and event observation behavior (lines 494-531). Both named receive methods keep cancellation/deadline checks, seed handling, empty-input behavior, and polling order around the refactor (lines 496-573). The new EOF reducer uses non-short-circuit boolean accumulation, so it continues through open queues and preserves first-error propagation in queue order, matching the prior Result<Vec<_>> collection behavior (lines 355-362). The patch removes the temporary Arc-vector clone and the temporary closed-state vector. Benchmark additions are separate and are not assessed as product performance evidence here.
verification: Read-only source inspection; no Cargo, tests, build, or timing run was performed, per instruction. Existing focused cursor tests were inspected but not executed.
limitations: This review does not establish a speedup or a whole-application runtime improvement.
This review does not independently verify benchmark validity or CI results.
